methodology.scope: AI events that happened and were reported inside the June 1-30, 2026 window.
methodology.selection: Fifty events ranked for a blend of capability impact, deployment reach, capital and infrastructure significance, policy consequence, security relevance, and societal friction.
methodology.verification: Each included event has at least one link to a trusted source named in instructions/blog.research.news.md. Aggregations and corporate announcements are labeled by source and publication date.
methodology.limitations: Some source sites exposed archives or search-index snippets rather than stable article pages, and several outlets limited crawling. No event was treated as verified solely from an inaccessible source.

clusters.name: Frontier models under border control
clusters.description: Model launches, export controls, state review, and the emerging contest over who gets access to frontier capability.

clusters.name: Agents at work
clusters.description: Agents moving from chat surfaces into software repositories, enterprise workflows, regulated systems, and long-running execution.

clusters.name: The compute frontier becomes a utility war
clusters.description: Capital, chips, memory, power, water, and sovereign infrastructure constraining the next phase of AI deployment.

clusters.name: Open models and the price of intelligence
clusters.description: Open weights, local inference, model efficiency, consumer surfaces, and new attempts to turn capability into defensible products.

clusters.name: The proof problem
clusters.description: Security incidents, evaluations, observability, labor friction, public resistance, and the evidence needed to trust autonomous systems.
